letters.title: The Navarrete parish registers
letters.to: Archivo Histórico Diocesano de Logroño (La Rioja, Spain)
letters.address: NOT YET VERIFIED — must be looked up on the diocese's own site before sending. This archive never guesses an address.
letters.lang: Spanish, with an English note offered
letters.subject: Consulta genealógica — partidas de la familia LERENA de Navarrete, c. 1840-1880
letters.why: The only place this archive can name where LERENA y LERENA was settled local usage. FamilySearch has not filmed the registers: the catalogue for Navarrete returns one subject, Census, and one item, the 1752 Catastro. Nothing is online. This is the only route.
letters.body:
Estimados señores:

Les escribo desde Sudáfrica para una investigación genealógica familiar, no académica, y les pido disculpas de antemano por las molestias.

Busco a una familia LERENA de NAVARRETE (La Rioja). Lo que sé de ella procede de un solo documento, otorgado lejos de allí: una escritura de poder firmada el 14 de noviembre de 1900 ante el Consulado de España en Buenos Aires (folio 138, escritura nº 368), en la que comparecen

    Don PRUDENCIO BENITO y Don JUAN JOSÉ LERENA Y LERENA,
    hermanos, mayores de edad, solteros, dependientes,
    NATURALES DE NAVARRETE, PROVINCIA DE LOGROÑO,

otorgando poder a su madre, Doña ISABELA LERENA Y BASARÁN, viuda, y mencionando a un tercer hermano, Don JOSÉ DOLORES LERENA Y LERENA, casado y residente en el pueblo. Juan José habría nacido hacia 1876.

Lo que me interesa es que los hijos llevan el apellido DUPLICADO como apellido de registro — Lerena y Lerena — lo que indica que el padre y la madre eran ambos Lerena. En los registros americanos que estudio esa combinación aparece casi siempre como error de copia; Navarrete es el único lugar que he podido nombrar donde parece ser real.

Quisiera preguntarles, si fuera posible:

1. ¿Se conservan en ese Archivo los libros parroquiales de Navarrete (bautismos y matrimonios) de aproximadamente 1820 a 1890, y están abiertos a consulta?

2. ¿Consta en ellos el MATRIMONIO de un LERENA con una LERENA celebrado en Navarrete antes de 1876 aproximadamente — presumiblemente los padres de los tres hermanos citados, siendo la esposa Isabela Lerena y Basarán, ya viuda en 1900?

3. ¿Y los BAUTISMOS de Prudencio Benito, Juan José y José Dolores Lerena y Lerena, hacia 1870-1880?

No les pido que realicen una búsqueda extensa. Si existe un índice, o un servicio de copias con sus tarifas, me basta con que me indiquen el procedimiento y estaré encantado de abonar los gastos que correspondan.

Si les resulta más cómodo, puedo escribir en inglés.

Les agradezco de antemano su tiempo y su atención.

Atentamente,

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com

letters.title: TAYLOR of Bideford — a first message to a fellow researcher
letters.to: RootsChat member "Welsh Jen", via the forum's private message system
letters.address: No email. The RootsChat Surname Interests Table lists her for TAYLOR of Bideford, Devon. SENDING REQUIRES AN ACCOUNT AND TWO FORUM POSTS before the PM system unlocks.
letters.subject: TAYLOR of Bideford — I have a good deal to share
letters.why: Bideford is the exact registration district of William Taylor and Mary Ann Helena Brayley and seven of their ten children. Offer first and ask second: this archive holds far more than it needs, and that is the right way round for a first message.
letters.body:
Hello,

I saw your TAYLOR of Bideford interest on the Surname Interests Table. I have been working on the same family and I would rather offer than ask, so here is what I hold, free to you whether or not any of it is yours.

WILLIAM TAYLOR and MARY ANN HELENA BRAYLEY, of Bideford, Devon. I have all TEN of their children with dates, six of the marriages with GRO volume and page references, the family in the 1891, 1901, 1911 and 1921 censuses, and the 1939 Register. The Northam, St Margaret baptism register covers several of the children.

The reason I am on it at all is the daughter who left: MARY SEPTIMA TAYLOR, born at Bideford on 17 September 1884, who married an Argentine and died at Cape Town on 15 November 1935. Her husband is my line, and she is the reason a Devon family turns up in a South American archive.

If any of that is your branch I will send it all over in whatever form is useful — I have it as transcriptions with citations rather than as a tree, so it should be easy to check rather than just believe.

What I am short of, if you happen to have it: anything on the BRAYLEY side before Mary Ann Helena, and anything on what became of the Taylor children who stayed in Devon after 1939.

No obligation at all — I am glad to send the material either way.

With thanks,
David Defranceski

letters.title: Chaser — the consular matrícula and the 1940 passport file
letters.to: Archivo Histórico de Cancillería, Buenos Aires

letters.subject: Reiteración de consulta — matrícula consular y expediente de pasaporte de PABLO ARMANDO LERENA (consulta del 9 de septiembre de 2026)
letters.why: Sent 9 September 2026 and unanswered after five weeks. This remains the single most likely document anywhere to name Juan Carlos and María Lerena, because the papers he produced in 1940 to prove his nationality may be the only surviving statement of his parentage.
letters.body:
Estimados señores:

Me permito reiterar, con todo respeto, una consulta genealógica que les dirigí el 9 de septiembre de 2026 y a la que aún no he recibido respuesta. Entiendo perfectamente que el Archivo atiende muchas solicitudes y que los plazos son los que son; si la mía está en trámite, les ruego que consideren este mensaje únicamente como una señal de que sigo interesado.

El caso, en resumen: busco la MATRÍCULA CONSULAR y el EXPEDIENTE DE PASAPORTE de

    PABLO ARMANDO LERENA, nacido el 22 de febrero de 1882,
    pasaporte argentino expedido en CIUDAD DEL CABO en 1940,
    fallecido allí en 1950.

Lo que más me importa es una sola cosa: QUÉ DOCUMENTOS PRESENTÓ PARA ACREDITAR SU NACIONALIDAD, y si esos documentos NOMBRAN A SUS PADRES.

El motivo es que no he podido hallar su partida de nacimiento por ningún otro camino. He revisado el registro de bautismos de la catedral de Rosario acta por acta para 1881, 1882 y 1883 — era la única parroquia de la ciudad hasta 1888 —, el registro civil uruguayo, los índices argentinos y españoles, y el censo nacional de 1895, en el que no figura. En Santa Fe no existía registro civil provincial en 1882. De modo que los papeles que él mismo presentó en 1940 podrían ser la única constancia que sobrevive de su filiación.

Quedo a su entera disposición para cualquier aclaración, y desde luego dispuesto a abonar los gastos de reproducción que correspondan.

Con mi agradecimiento por su tiempo,

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com

letters.subject: Reiteración de consulta — legajo de PABLO ARMANDO LERENA, clase 1882, enrolado en Ciudad del Cabo, 1908
letters.why: Sent 8 September 2026 and unanswered after five weeks. The enrolment card is the one document on earth that names Juan Carlos and María Lerena; any service file behind it would be the second.
letters.body:
Estimados señores:

Me permito reiterar una consulta genealógica que les dirigí el 8 de septiembre de 2026 y a la que todavía no he recibido respuesta. Si ya está en trámite, les ruego disculpen la insistencia y tomen este mensaje sólo como constancia de mi interés.

Busco cualquier legajo o documentación de servicio correspondiente a

    PABLO ARMANDO LERENA, CLASE 1882,
    ficha de enrolamiento de la Oficina enroladora de CIUDAD DEL CABO (Sudáfrica),
    Serie E 3555, Sección I 3322,
    Cajón 985 de las fichas de enrolamiento.

Su ficha consigna como padres a JUAN CARLOS LERENA y a MARÍA LERENA, y como lugar de nacimiento ROSARIO DE SANTA FE.

Lo que me interesa, concretamente, es si existe detrás de esa ficha ALGÚN EXPEDIENTE que amplíe esos datos — y en particular si en él consta la partida de nacimiento que debió presentar, o cualquier dato adicional sobre sus padres.

Explico el motivo: esos dos nombres aparecen en esa ficha y, hasta donde he podido comprobar, EN NINGÚN OTRO DOCUMENTO CONOCIDO. He buscado en los registros parroquiales de Rosario acta por acta, en el registro civil uruguayo, en los índices argentinos y españoles y en el censo de 1895. La ficha es, por ahora, la única constancia de su filiación.

Quedo a su disposición y dispuesto a abonar los gastos que correspondan.

Con mi agradecimiento,

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com

letters.title: Follow-up — the will and inventory, not the death notice
letters.to: Western Cape Archives and Records Service, Cape Town
letters.address: archives.clientservices@westerncape.gov.za — ALREADY VERIFIED and used on 10 September 2026.
letters.subject: Estate MOOC 6/9/17017 — follow-up request for the will and inventory
letters.why: The original request asked for the death notice. That turned up in David's own files on 16 September and gives both parents as NOT KNOWN. What is still worth having from the estate file is different: the will of 6 February 1942 and the inventory.
letters.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I wrote to you on 10 September 2026 about estate file MOOC 6/9/17017 (PABLO ARMANDO LERENA, died Cape Town 1950). I am writing to narrow that request rather than to repeat it, because part of it has since been answered from another source.

I no longer need the DEATH NOTICE. A photograph of it turned up in our own family papers; it records both parents as "not known", and the informant was not a relative.

What I would still very much like, if they survive in the file, are:

1. The WILL, dated 6 February 1942; and
2. The INVENTORY of the estate.

My interest in them is genealogical rather than financial. The deceased was born in Argentina in 1882 and his parentage is not recorded anywhere I have been able to find — the death notice itself says as much. A will often names relatives that no official form asks for, and an inventory sometimes lists papers, photographs or documents brought from abroad. Either could carry a name I cannot otherwise reach.

I would be grateful if you could tell me the procedure and the cost of copies, and I am happy to pay the usual fees.

With thanks for your time,

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com

letters.subject: Request for the personnel record of NUNO FERNANDO LERENA, born 6 October 1924 (South African Air Force; possibly 12 Squadron)
letters.why: A 1997 letter says Nuno 'served in the Western Desert' in the Air Force, and a 1971 death notice is signed '12th Squadron, S.A.A.F.'. Neither gives a service record. The Documentation Centre holds the personnel files of former Union Defence Force members, and this is the one document that would settle both the service and the unit. NEEDS FROM YOU BEFORE IT GOES: your postal address and signature; copies of his death and birth certificates (both are on his page); your own ID; and, if they ask for it, a signed consent from one of Nuno's children, who are living and are not named here. A shorter email version is in David's Gmail drafts, addressed to archive@dod.mil.za and not sent; the Centre says records cannot be sent electronically, so a postal address has to be in whichever version goes. *** A short email version of this request was SENT on 16 October 2026 *** (see the errand above); this fuller postal version has not been, and stays here as the fallback if the email bounces or is not answered.
letters.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing as the grandson of the late NUNO FERNANDO LERENA, to ask whether the Department of Defence Archives holds a personnel file for him and, if it does, to request a copy under the Promotion of Access to Information Act.

What I know about him:

    Full name:       Nuno Fernando LERENA (known as "Larry")
    Born:            6 October 1924, Wynberg, Cape Town
    Identity no.:    331 406051 W (as it appears on his 1958 identity card and on the
                     estate death notice; his death certificate has it written 331-406057,
                     so please search on both)
    Died:            1 July 1971, Germiston
    Wife:            Catherine Mary Sophia LERENA, born Booyzen (deceased)

What I believe about his service, and what I do not know:

    - I believe he served in the South African Air Force in the Second World War. A
      relative's letter of 1997 says he "joined the Air Force and served in the Western
      Desert", and a notice in the newspaper after his death was signed "12th Squadron,
      S.A.A.F."
    - I do not know his service or force number, his rank, his trade, or the dates of his
      service. I cannot say whether the squadron named was his in the war or later.

What I would be grateful for, in this order:

    1. Confirmation of whether a personnel file exists for him.
    2. If it does, a copy of the file; or, failing that, the basic particulars it holds -
       service number, units and dates, rank, discharge details and any awards.
    3. Please tell me what you require from me: the proof of relationship, the written
       consent of next of kin if you need it, and the copying fee. I will arrange all three.

I enclose a copy of his death certificate and of his birth certificate. I understand that records are not sent electronically, so I would be glad of a reply and any copies by post to the address below.

With thanks for your help,

[Your name, as you sign it]
[Your postal address]
[Your telephone]
david.defranceski@gmail.com

Enclosures: death certificate (A 243689); birth certificate (A 042921); [copy of your identity document]; [consent of next of kin, if you are told it is needed]
